{{Use American English|date = June 2021}}
{{Short description|Theorem about holomorphic functions of several complex variables}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Bochner's tube theorem''' (named for [[Salomon Bochner]]) shows that every function holomorphic on a [[tube domain]] in <math>\mathbb{C}^n</math> can be extended to the [[convex hull]] of this domain. 

'''Theorem''' Let <math>\omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n</math> be a connected [[open set]]. Then every function <math>f(z)</math> holomorphic on the [[tube domain]] <math> \Omega = \omega+i \mathbb{R}^n</math> can be extended to a function holomorphic on the convex hull <math>\operatorname{ch}(\Omega)</math>.

A classic reference is {{harvtxt|Bochner|Martin|1948}}<ref name="Bochner Martin Haar 1948 p. ">{{cite book | last1=Bochner | first1=S. | last2=Martin | first2=W.T.| title=Several Complex Variables | publisher=Princeton University Press | series=Princeton mathematical series | year=1948}}</ref> (Theorem 9). See also {{harvtxt|Hounie|2009}}<ref name="Hounie 2009">{{cite journal | last=Hounie | first=J. | title=A Proof of Bochner's Tube Theorem | journal=Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society | publisher=American Mathematical Society | volume=137 | issue=12 | year=2009 | pages=4203–4207 | doi=10.1090/S0002-9939-09-10057-6 | jstor=40590656 | doi-access=free }}</ref> and {{harvtxt|Noguchi|2020}}<ref>{{cite arXiv |eprint=2007.04597|last1=Noguchi|first1=Junjiro|title=A brief proof of Bochner's tube theorem and a generalized tube|year=2020|class=math.CV}}</ref> for other proofs.

== Generalizations ==

The generalized version of this theorem was first proved by Kazlow (1979),<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-1979-0542875-5|title=CR functions and tube manifolds|year=1979|last1=Kazlow|first1=M.|journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society|volume=255|page=153|doi-access=free}}</ref> also proved by Boivin and Dwilewicz (1998)<ref>{{cite journal |jstor=117646|title=Extension and Approximation of CR Functions on Tube Manifolds|last1=Boivin|first1=André|last2=Dwilewicz|first2=Roman|journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society|year=1998|volume=350|issue=5|pages=1945–1956|doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-98-02019-4|doi-access=free}}.</ref> under more less complicated hypothese.

'''Theorem''' Let <math>\omega</math> be a connected [[submanifold]] of <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math> of [[Smoothness|class]]-<math>C^2</math>. Then every continuous [[CR function]] on the tube domain <math>\Omega(\omega)</math> can be continuously extended to a CR function on <math>\Omega(\text{ach}(\omega)).\ \left(\Omega(\omega) = \omega+i \mathbb{R}^n\subset\mathbb{C}^n\ \left(n\geq 2\right), \text{ach}(\omega):=\omega\cup \text{Int}\ \text{ch}(\omega)\right)</math>. By "Int ch(S)" we will mean the interior taken in the smallest dimensional space which contains "ch(S)".
